description: Programmable cellular automata for inventing societies and watching them emerge.
readme:
# Game of Society

**Write local rules. Watch societies emerge.**

Game of Society is a browser-based programmable cellular automaton. Give cells properties such as age, wealth or opinion, write JavaScript rules for how neighbours interact, and watch societies emerge.

**[▶ Play Game of Society](https://gameofsociety.alirizasaral.com/)**

[![Game of Society running in a desktop browser](game-of-society.png)](https://gameofsociety.alirizasaral.com/)

## Try a society

### Aging Conway Society

Conway-style cells also have an age, showing how one additional dimension changes a familiar cellular automaton. **[Play Aging Conway Society](https://gameofsociety.alirizasaral.com/?preset=aging)**

### Majority Drift

Cells respond to the local distribution of neighbouring groups, producing larger-scale patterns from local imitation. **[Play Majority Drift](https://gameofsociety.alirizasaral.com/?preset=majority)**

### Cyclic Tribes

Locally competing states create moving boundaries and recurring patterns. **[Play Cyclic Tribes](https://gameofsociety.alirizasaral.com/?preset=cyclic)**

## Write your own rules

`cell` contains the current dimensions, `neighbors` contains the eight surrounding cells, and the function returns the cell's complete next state.

```javascript
function update(cell, neighbors) {
  const living = neighbors.filter(n => n && n.alive).length;
  return {
    alive: cell.alive
      ? living === 2 || living === 3
      : living === 3
  };
}
```

Change a few lines, press play, and see what kind of society the rule creates.

## Essentials

- Choose a built-in world or create your own.
- Define dimensions such as age, wealth, tribe, opinion or happiness.
- Write transition and display rules in JavaScript.
- Inspect, paint, randomize, pause, step and rewind.
- Save configurations locally and share worlds through URLs.
- Run the application locally without a build system.

## Run locally

Clone the repository and open `game-of-society.html` in a recent browser. No installation or build step is required.

The supported mobile baseline is Safari 16.4+ on iPhone. Other recent Chromium and Firefox browsers are supported too. A larger screen is more comfortable for writing custom rules.

## Why Game of Society?

Simple local rules can generate surprising global behaviour. No cell sees the whole grid or plans the final pattern, yet waves, borders, cycles and collapses appear.

Here, cells are more than alive or dead. They can carry an age, wealth, profession, opinion, identity or level of happiness, opening many more kinds of worlds.

Game of Society is a mathematical toy and a game, not a serious policy-modelling tool. History and sociology offer inspiration, not claims that a colourful grid accurately models humanity.

The rules may be sensible, absurd or deliberately unfair. Their consequences are the entertainment.

The code is simple. The spectacle is not.

**[Read the full idea behind Game of Society →](ABOUT.md)**

## Contributing

New society ideas, rule experiments and focused improvements are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the short guide.
